result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A uses a clean table sorted by due date with fully paid invoices left off. Its status labels are in words ('Overdue 10 days'), amounts are right-aligned with two decimals and the currency is stated in the column headers, and the part-paid invoice shows its total, the amount received and the balance. B is also well ordered, groups invoices into sections and handles the part payment clearly, but its card layout puts dates inline instead of in their own columns, and its amounts don't form a true aligned column the way a table's would. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers leave out paid invoices, sort overdue first and label each one with how many days overdue it is. B puts the amounts in right-aligned numeric columns that line up on the decimal point, shows invoice total, amount received and balance due for the part-paid invoice, and keeps the due date in its own column. A uses cards, so the amounts don't sit in one column and the dates are folded into a text line with the issue date; B is easier to scan at a glance.
